title: Proximity-based latency gradient and NetIndex routing policy with tier-aware fallbacks
creator: Priya Patel
description: Introduce a runnable routing policy (ProxLat + NetIndex) that fuses latency percentiles (p50, p95) with an aggregated link-quality score (NetIndex) to pick region/tier and select fallback model variants. Goal: reduce user-visible tail latency and failure-induced fallbacks by preferring POPs with strong short-term p95 behavior while avoiding noisy links (packet loss/jitter). Policy must be configurable per customer tier and support safe canary rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: A scoring library (proxlat_netindex) implemented and published to infra/routers as an importable module
Router evaluates candidate POPs using weighted score: 0.6*p95_norm + 0.3*p50_norm + 0.1*(1-NetIndex) by default with runtime-config overrides
Config layer supports per-customer tier weight overrides and hard exclusion lists
End-to-end tests demonstrating fallback to compatible model variants when chosen POP cannot serve within latency SLO
Perf overhead of policy evaluation < 3% CPU on router hot path and adds < 1ms median decision latency
Console dashboard tile showing: score time-series, top-k POPs per-customer, and canary rollout heatmap
Canary rollout plan validated: 1% traffic -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% with automatic halt on p95 regression > 15%

design_decisions: Use percentile smoothing with EWMA on p50/p95 windows to reduce oscillation (window=60s, alpha=0.2)
NetIndex aggregates packet_loss_ewma and jitter_ms_ewma into a 0..1 health score using tuned thresholds instead of raw values
Default weights biased toward p95 to prioritize tail reduction for interactive workloads; weights are runtime-configurable per customer tier
Fallback model selection uses compatibility matrix and prefers smaller, faster variants only when latency SLO risk is high; full fallbacks tracked in console
Scoring is deterministic for identical inputs to ensure reproducible canaries and A/B comparisons
tradeoffs: Heavier reliance on p95 increases sensitivity to transient tail spikes; mitigated with EWMA smoothing but may delay reacting to real regressions
Adding NetIndex prevents selection of noisy links but requires additional telemetry and ingestion cost
Tier-aware overrides allow enterprise customers to pin to specific regions at the expense of global latency optimization
Deterministic scoring simplifies analysis but may reduce exploration diversity for multi-pop routing strategies
